output.summary: Annual herb considered native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia, though its precise origin is uncertain. Its vivid red, four-petalled flowers usually have black basal spots, last only one day, and can reappear from a long-lived seed bank after soil disturbance. The black seeds are edible alone or in bread, although most culinary poppy seed comes from another species.
output.edibilityNote: Black seeds are eaten alone or in bread; most poppy seed harvested for cooking comes from Papaver somniferum.
